title: Runtime descriptor
description: How the runner attaches to one runtime and turns its records into session events. A descriptor matches and copies; it never computes. runtimes/<name>/descriptor.yaml, with fixtures beside it.

version.description: The descriptor format. A runner refuses a version it does not read.

runtime.description: The runtime this describes, as the launch spec sets it: claude, codex.

title.description: The runtime's display name: Claude Code. runtimes.json lists it beside the name.

runtime_version.description: The runtime version the rules were written against and the fixtures recorded from. Reported in run.started; the runner never checks the installed version.

sources.description: How the runner attaches. The terminal bytes are always captured and need no source: there is nothing in them to match.

output.description: Structured output on the runtime's standard output, when the session runs on pipes.

format.description: jsonl: one JSON object per line. Lines that are not JSON objects are not records.

hooks.description: Hook calls the runtime makes. The runner installs its forwarder as a command hook for each listed event in the settings the launch passes; the forwarder writes what it reads on its standard input to the local socket as one record.

install.description: How the runner installs its forwarder, chosen among the ways the binary implements. claude-settings: a command hook per event, added to the JSON settings file the launch passes with --settings, or to a new one when it passes none.

events.description: The runtime's hook event names to install the forwarder for, in the runtime's own spelling.

stop.description: How the runner stops the runtime, at a run's time limit or when the runner itself is stopped. Runtimes differ in what a signal means, one closes its session on SIGINT and drops it on SIGTERM, and this sets which the runtime gets. A run that sets a signal or a grace of its own overrides it; absent, SIGTERM and ten seconds.

signal.description: The signal that requests the runtime's exit, among the ones the runner sends.

grace.description: How long the runtime has after the signal before SIGKILL, as a duration: 30s.

headless.description: The arguments that mean the runtime runs without an interface. When one of them is among the arguments the runtime is started with, the session runs on pipes even at a terminal, exactly as when the caller requests pipes: the runtime is recorded as not interactive and the output source is read. Absent, the caller alone decides.

args.description: The arguments, each as the runtime spells it. A short one matches the whole token (-p); a long one matches the token or its --name=value form (--print, --print=...). Nothing else is inferred: a runtime that takes its prompt on standard input has no argument to list, and its caller sets headless itself.

secrets.description: The secrets the runtime needs and the variables it keeps for itself. runtimes.json lists the secrets of every descriptor the contract ships.

declares.description: The secrets the runtime reads, each from one variable, and where the proxy sets each value.

id.description: The declaration's id, unique among the declarations.

title.description: What the secret is, for a person choosing one.

name.description: The variable the runtime reads the secret from.

hosts.description: The hosts the value is set on: exact DNS names, no wildcard, no IP literal.

paths.description: The paths of those hosts the value is set on, in the policy's path grammar. Absent means every path.

auth.description: How the value is set on a request, a scheme from the closed set. The declaration's own value is the one secret it sets, so auth contains neither secret nor username_secret.

one_of.description: Groups of declarations, of which at most one each applies. of lists declared ids, each id in at most one group. A required group needs one; a declaration in no group is optional.

reserves.description: Variables the runtime reads a credential from beside the declared ones. Behind a wall, a declared or reserved variable that neither a placeholder, the run nor the runtime's preparation sets goes in empty.

denies.description: Variables the runner always leaves out of the server's set for the runtime, and reports: the ones that move where the runtime sends its requests and credentials, or change what it runs.

credential_files.description: Files in which the runtime keeps a credential of its own, ~ being the home of the user the runner runs as.

rules.description: Evaluated in order against every record of the rule's source; the first rule whose match succeeds produces one event, and a record no rule matches produces nothing.

match.description: Every entry must match: a path into the record equals the value, a string, number or boolean; or, with {present: true}, the path exists. Nothing else: no patterns, no ranges, no expressions.

data.description: The event's data: each key is a field of the type's data, each value a dotted path into the record whose value is copied there unchanged. A path that does not exist leaves the field out.
